title: Timed Insight (overlay stream item)
description: One machine-readable item in the live insight stream. Only verified claims become insights. The stream says WHAT to show and WHEN; the frontend owns which widget draws each insight_type. Suitable for rendering as a synchronized overlay on a match feed.

start_sec.description: Match clock when the overlay appears.

duration_sec.description: How long it stays on screen.

emitted_latency_ms.description: Time from triggering event to emission, for latency monitoring.

insight_type.description: Semantic type. The frontend maps it to a widget; the backend never names widgets.

player_ids.description: Players the insight involves. Used by player-focus mode to filter the stream.

claim_id.description: The verified claim this insight was built from.

context_chip.description: Present when status is published_with_context: the shallow standard stat shown muted beside the honest insight.

payload.description: Data for the widget, shape depends on insight_type. See docs/contracts.md for per-type shapes. Coordinates use a 0-100 by 0-100 pitch, always from the attacking team's point of view (attacking toward x=100).

focus.description: Viewport hint for the Focus Pitch.

points.description: Event-based path or markers (only provable events).

value.description: e.g. xT added or xG for this event.

series.description: e.g. rhythm waveform, one point per minute for the last 15 minutes.

family.description: tactical_pattern: the pattern family (pat_*) shown; for a revised naive claim, the family its trap rule belongs to.

claim_metric.description: tactical_pattern: the claim's metric (a pat_* family, or the naive metric a trap rule revised).

window.description: tactical_pattern: the match clock span the claim covers.

text.description: Text is rendered from the verified claim's template_key + params. Translation happens after verification; the number guard confirms every numeric param still appears in each translation.

rendered.description: language code -> tone -> text. Tones: 'analyst' (tactical language) and 'casual' (plain language).
